The strongest next experiment remains **terminal endpoint sampling**: replace the proposed branch-allocation change with one controlled change inside BERT4Rec’s terminal sampler.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** First, snapshots report equal branch sizes and 0.5/0.5 coefficients, while definitions describe different interventions; provenance must be resolved before attribution. Second, measured terminal endpoint exposure is approximately 10%. Raising it tests a different distribution of historical prediction problems, not merely more recent attention. Third, sampled-negative error rates below 7% coexist with Electronics selection HR@10 of 0.465; these measure different tasks and establish no intervention gain.

**Insights from related work.** BERT4Rec [1] already supplements random masking with final-item masking, limiting novelty; its context-length and masking experiments also show dataset dependence. RSS [4] motivates graded recency, but changes models and target sampling, so it does not validate this intervention. Replication research [2] identifies convergence as a competing explanation. Sampled-metric research [5] limits conclusions to the pinned candidate protocol, while adaptive-analysis research [6] cautions that validation reuse creates selection optimism.

Three directions remain: supervision allocation, objective emphasis, and terminal-context selection. The framework separates **how many views**, **how strongly losses contribute**, and **which historical prediction problems are learned**:

| Candidate | Controlled change | Originality / potential / difficulty | Positive; negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bernoulli terminal allocation [1] | Terminal-view probability 0.75 | 2 / 5 / 4 | Simple sampling change; separate normalization complicates interpretation |
| Terminal objective emphasis [1] | Loss weights 0.25/0.75 | 3 / 6 / 3 | Explicit emphasis; may weaken reconstruction |
| **Endpoint sampling** [1,3] | Endpoint probability 0.10→0.50 | **2 / 5 / 3** | Atomic context-distribution test; concentrates target exposure |
| Graded recency [4] | Smooth cutoff weighting | 3 / 6 / 3 | Retains diverse prefixes; adds an unsupported schedule choice |

At 30% progress, retain endpoint sampling for feasibility. Preserve fixed paired branches, separate target means and baseline coefficients. For history length n>2, choose final index n−1 with probability 0.50; otherwise choose uniformly from 1…n−2. For n=2, choose index 1. Exclude the target and later events, append reserved MASK, and preserve reconstruction.

Pseudocode: `j = sample_endpoint_or_interior(history); sequence = left_pad(history[max(0,j-L+1):j] + [MASK]); terminal_loss = CE(sequence, history[j]); optimize(original_combined_loss)`.

Persist probabilities, cutoff counts, context lengths, target exposure and checkpoint provenance. This intervention intentionally changes both context lengths and target frequencies; it cannot isolate either mechanism. Retain all four categories, one checkpoint each, seeds, limits, predictor generation and diagnostic interfaces. Read the maximum nonpadding position.

Prespecify 0.50, checkpoint cadence and selection rules; record every inspected checkpoint/trial. Selection remains pinned macro validation HR@10. Report category changes and history-length diagnostics when supported by supplied outcomes; paired user bootstrap intervals remain descriptive after selection. Recent-context perturbations [3] can assess sensitivity, not intent. Endpoint memorization is a risk hypothesis, not a demonstrated finding. No supplied result establishes improvement, full-catalog gains, ownership, compatibility or mood.

idea.description: Prespecify full-training-history endpoint probability 0.50 within the corrected BERT4Rec terminal sampler, replacing the proposed terminal-branch allocation intervention. Preserve fixed paired reconstruction/terminal views and the baseline's separately normalized 0.5/0.5 objective. Train exactly one independent BERT4Rec model per category. Treat this as a controlled change to terminal target-position sampling, with intentionally changed target exposure and context-length distributions.
idea.motivation: Supplied measured protocols describe endpoint probability 0.10 despite appended-MASK inference using the complete available history. A 0.50 endpoint probability tests whether more frequent supervision on training-history endings improves the pinned next-item ranking metric. BERT4Rec already includes final-item masking, so the contribution is a local sampling experiment rather than a new modeling principle. Complete training histories are shorter than the histories available at validation prediction and need not represent the same distribution; retaining interior targets preserves varied prediction contexts. RSS provides adjacent motivation for balancing recency and coverage, without establishing the best distribution for BERT4Rec. Neither the chosen probability nor endpoint-induced memorization is established by the supplied evidence. At 30% progress, retain this simple intervention rather than simultaneously changing allocation, loss weights, context length or mask density.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate only the terminal cutoff policy below into the host-supplied corrected baseline. Its executable source is absent from the prompt, so this is an integration specification, not a standalone replacement train.py. The selected intervention supersedes p_terminal_branch=0.75 and terminal-loss-weight=0.75; do not combine them. The supplied snapshots and definitions conflict, and repeated numerical results do not establish that either prior intervention actually ran. Bind the actual executable configuration, sampler identity, objective coefficients and measured counters to the selected checkpoint. Use the supplied corrected baseline as the implementation authority and disclose any discrepancy with the assumed 0.10 endpoint policy before interpreting a coefficient- or sampler-only comparison.

Use zero-based target index j. Eligible indices are 1..n-1, guaranteeing at least one preceding event. For n>2, P(j=n-1)=0.50 and P(j=k)=0.50/(n-2) for k=1..n-2. For n=2, j=1 deterministically. For n=3, the proposed distribution is uniform over the two eligible targets; for longer histories it increasingly concentrates probability at the endpoint relative to uniform target-index sampling. The comparison is against the documented endpoint probability 0.10, not against a universally uniform baseline. Construct terminal input from history[max(0,j-(L-1)):j] followed by reserved MASK, then left-pad to L. Exclude the target position and every later event; an earlier occurrence of the same item ID remains legitimate historical context. Retain baseline positional IDs and reconstruction masking and fallback behavior.

Preserve baseline branch sizes, branch-conditional user sampling, total processed views, loss reductions, coefficients, optimizer, clipping, validation cadence, tie handling and stopping rules. The supplied configuration describes 64 sequences per branch, batch size 128, maxlen 128, hidden width 64, two blocks, two heads, dropout 0.2, Adam learning rate 0.001, zero weight decay, clipping at 5, evaluation every five epochs, patience 20 and earliest maximum category validation HR@10. Preserve the executable corrected baseline if documentation differs, recording the actual settings. Preserve its empty-branch behavior rather than introducing a new fallback or exception policy. Keep catalog CE over real items, with tied item embeddings and PAD/MASK excluded from output classes.

The pseudocode illustrates the distribution using a NumPy Generator. At integration, retain the baseline RNG API and draw structure where possible: change the existing endpoint threshold rather than replacing its generator or reseeding. Do not claim identical masks or user streams solely because seed 42 is fixed; conditional cutoff draws can advance a shared RNG differently. Preserve established independent purpose streams if present. Record whether the intervention changes downstream random draws; adding new streams would itself require disclosure. The policy helpers must not become a replacement preprocessing pipeline.

This experiment deliberately changes terminal target-item frequencies, repeated endpoint exposure and context-length distributions. It therefore does not isolate recent-item attention, context length, target identity, calendar recency or memorization. Do not add importance weighting, which would change the intended objective. Equal branch sizes preserve terminal target counts per update; reconstruction target counts can remain stochastic under the unchanged masking procedure. Record realized counts rather than claiming all target counts are identical. Separately normalized branch losses keep their scalar coefficients; those coefficients do not equal gradient shares. Preserving updates per epoch does not guarantee equal realized compute or total updates when stopping times differ.

Keep Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preprocessing seed is 0 and training seed is 42. Use one GPU, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per completed epoch. Respect the host's SASREC_EPOCHS=200 default despite the variable name. Save artifacts beneath the trial directory and charge training, diagnostics, debugging and failures to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Do not fetch data or pretrained weights, access hidden test files, inspect other trials, reuse their checkpoints, or change splits or the host evaluator.

Persist endpoint/interior counts, expected endpoint counts conditional on sampled history lengths, actual target probabilities, target-item exposure counts, context-length histograms, detached branch CE sums, exact denominators, objective coefficients, weighted contributions and selected-epoch provenance. Identify whether records cover the selected epoch, cumulative updates through selection or the entire completed run. Report pooled CE sums divided by pooled target counts separately from mean batch objectives. Definitions must be generated from the measured configuration and records, with unavailable measurements null. Do not describe a fixed 64/64 sampler as Bernoulli allocation or a 0.5/0.5 objective as 0.25/0.75.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Preserve sample_batch and ModelView interfaces, including actual nn.Module view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data; loader tensors remain B x L. Diagnostic final-position coverage cannot identify training branch allocation or full-history endpoint exposure. Restore model mode after evaluation probes, exclude PAD/MASK from item geometry and validate finite scores and expected shapes.

Architecture and inference remain baseline BERT4Rec. Keep the predictor writer consistent with checkpoint architecture, configuration, item mapping, reserved MASK ID and positional conventions. Append MASK after at most L-1 history events, left-pad and read the maximum nonpadding position, never count-1. Each category loads exactly one independently trained selected checkpoint, with no averaging, score fusion, separately fitted popularity/transition scores or auxiliary predictor. Retain full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for twenty training users, five per category, separately from sampled-candidate selection.

Selection uses the pinned macro validation HR@10 with 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. Prespecify 0.50 without a cutoff-probability sweep. Preserve the baseline checkpoint evaluation frequency, tie handling and stopping rule; log every inspected checkpoint and trial. Report category scores, equally weighted macro score, selected epochs, completed updates and GPU time. The supplied category selection scores average to 0.5975, but are not a verified endpoint-intervention result or an independently established host comparison. Report improvement only from an actual matched host comparison.

If the host supplies paired per-user hit outcomes for corrected baseline and intervention, resample user pairs independently within each category using a separate analysis RNG, retain both model outcomes and fixed candidates, and recompute the equally weighted macro difference for 10,000 bootstrap replicates. Report observed category and macro differences and percentile 95% intervals. Cluster repeated identities when applicable. Aggregate HR values alone cannot reconstruct these intervals. With 200 users/category, one additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fitted seed-42 models and fixed candidates; they exclude training-seed, candidate-resampling and dataset variability, and do not correct checkpoint-selection or search optimism. Leave final held-out assessment to the host.

For descriptive history-length analysis, predeclare bins, for example 1-5, 6-10, 11-20 and greater than 20 available pre-target history events. Report counts and paired category changes only when host-supplied outcomes and permitted history lengths support them; mark empty bins unavailable and do not tune bins after seeing results. Do not modify the evaluator to obtain missing outputs. If comparing training and validation performance, use matched appended-MASK prediction and candidate construction on training-history prefixes, exclude the target and later events, and disclose training-sample optimism. A reconstruction CE versus validation HR comparison is not a meaningful numerical generalization gap. Optional fixed training-prefix CE probes can instead describe endpoint/interior fitting separately, with counts and context distributions, without entering checkpoint selection.

Endpoint concentration may repeatedly expose a small set of user-ending targets, encourage item-frequency shortcuts or weaken learning across interior transitions; these are hypotheses requiring measurements. Target exposure logs, fixed prefix probes and optional frozen recent-deletion, count-matched random-deletion and latest-item-preserving shuffle controls can characterize behavior. Keep targets, candidates and MASK fixed across perturbations; rebuild padding consistently, use evaluation mode and an independent diagnostic RNG, and include identity controls. Report accuracy changes separately from ranking overlap, with user-clustered uncertainty where feasible. Sensitivity alone establishes neither useful context dependence nor causal intent. These probes consume the shared budget and must not become an adaptive validation tuning loop.

Only supplied histories, timestamps, titles and descriptions are usable; unavailable ratings, reviews, categories, prices, stores and simulator traits remain unknown. Histories alone establish neither equipment ownership nor unresolved demand. Qualitative feedback should distinguish explicit current acceptance, topical relation, explicit rejection and insufficient evidence; compatibility, duplication, quantities and mood require supporting evidence. No sampling intervention by itself resolves these semantic failures. Graded recency sampling, context-length changes and mask-density changes remain alternative future single-model experiments, each requiring its own prespecified comparison. No training, effectiveness, seed robustness or full-catalog improvement is asserted here.
idea.pseudocode:
import numpy as np


def sample_terminal_cutoff(history_length, rng):
    """Reference policy using the baseline's seeded NumPy Generator.

    Integration should change the existing cutoff threshold in place when
    possible, preserving its RNG API, streams and branch construction.
    """
    n = int(history_length)
    if n < 2:
        raise ValueError('Terminal supervision requires two training events')
    if n == 2:
        return 1
    if rng.random() < 0.50:
        return n - 1
    return int(rng.integers(1, n - 1))  # 1 through n-2, inclusive


def terminal_target_probability(history_length, target_index):
    n, j = int(history_length), int(target_index)
    if n < 2 or not 1 <= j < n:
        raise ValueError('Invalid terminal target')
    if n == 2:
        return 1.0
    return 0.50 if j == n - 1 else 0.50 / (n - 2)


def terminal_view(history, maxlen, mask_id, cutoff_rng):
    """history contains only the supplied user's training interactions.

    Reference construction; retain baseline mapping and positional rules.
    Earlier occurrences of the target item ID are legitimate context.
    """
    if maxlen < 2:
        raise ValueError('Need room for context and reserved MASK')
    j = sample_terminal_cutoff(len(history), cutoff_rng)
    context = history[max(0, j - (maxlen - 1)):j]
    sequence = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
    tokens = np.asarray(list(context) + [mask_id], dtype=np.int64)
    sequence[-len(tokens):] = tokens
    labels = np.zeros(maxlen, dtype=np.int64)
    labels[-1] = int(history[j])
    provenance = {
        'target_index': j,
        'history_length': len(history),
        'context_length': len(context),
        'is_endpoint': j == len(history) - 1,
        'target_probability': terminal_target_probability(len(history), j),
        'expected_endpoint_probability': 1.0 if len(history) == 2 else 0.50,
    }
    return sequence, labels, provenance


# Integration into each category's supplied corrected BERT4Rec baseline:
# 1. Record actual sampler, objective, RNG and checkpoint-selection semantics.
#    Resolve contradictory records; do not infer execution from definitions.
# 2. Preserve fixed reconstruction/terminal counts and baseline user streams.
#    Change only the terminal endpoint threshold from documented 0.10 to 0.50.
#    Record any downstream RNG divergence due to conditional cutoff draws.
# 3. Preserve reconstruction, catalog CE, denominators, 0.5/0.5 coefficients,
#    empty-branch policy, optimizer, clipping and checkpoint selection.
# 4. Persist measured cutoff, context, target-exposure and loss accounting,
#    tied to configuration and selected-checkpoint identity and interval.
# 5. Preserve all diagnostic interfaces; definitions describe actual records.
# 6. Save one selected checkpoint per category and generate its predictor.
#    Inference: left_pad(history[-(L-1):] + [MASK]); read max nonpadding index.
# 7. Keep four-category routing, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'],
#    preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs,
#    200 batches per completed epoch, one GPU and trial-local artifacts.
# 8. Host evaluates unchanged users/candidates and sampled HR@10.
#    Compare only with supplied matched baseline outcomes when available.
#    Optional paired user bootstrap is descriptive after model selection.
# No training or validation result is asserted by this integration code.

originality.positive: Separates terminal target-position sampling from allocation and objective coefficients, providing a clear local experiment within the required BERT4Rec family.
originality.negative: BERT4Rec already includes final-item masking, and endpoint oversampling is conventional; no matched prior study being supplied establishes novelty.

future_potential.positive: Can inform subsequent studies of target exposure, context distributions and graded recency while retaining a single BERT4Rec network.
future_potential.negative: The probability is unvalidated, the intervention couples multiple distributional changes, and it does not directly resolve compatibility or current-usefulness failures.

code_difficulty.positive: The model change is one sampling threshold with no backbone or inference architecture modification.
code_difficulty.negative: Reproducible integration requires resolving conflicting provenance, preserving RNG semantics, persisting measured accounting and checking checkpoint–predictor consistency.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item modeling for sequential recommendation and reserved-MASK next-item prediction.
Supplements random masked-item training with final-item masking, supporting inference alignment.
Reports dataset-dependent effects of context length and masking proportion.
limitations: Does not establish that endpoint probability 0.50 improves this corrected baseline or these four datasets.
Final-item masking is already part of the method, limiting the proposed intervention's novelty.
Masked reconstruction performance does not establish appended-MASK ranking quality.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec replication and training-convergence study
contributions: Identifies training convergence and implementation choices as important factors in BERT4Rec comparisons.
limitations: Does not validate the proposed terminal cutoff distribution or establish endpoint-induced memorization.
Its findings cannot replace measurements under the pinned RecHarness protocol and training limits.

related_work.title: Betello et al.: Sequential recommendation perturbation study
contributions: Studies recommendation sensitivity to interaction perturbations, including recent-interaction removal.
Motivates separating ranking stability from accuracy.
limitations: Training-data perturbation results do not directly establish frozen BERT4Rec inference behavior.
Sensitivity does not establish useful current-context dependence or justify the proposed sampling probability.

related_work.title: Recency-based Sampling of Sequences
contributions: Provides adjacent evidence that intermediate recency weighting can outperform endpoint-only continuation across studied settings.
Motivates graded recency as an alternative to concentrating all continuation supervision at endpoints.
limitations: The recency interventions train SASRec, GRU4Rec and Caser; BERT4Rec is a comparison baseline.
Multiple-target sampling and different model families prevent direct attribution to BERT4Rec terminal cutoff weighting.
Does not establish that graded recency or probability 0.50 is best under the pinned task.

related_work.title: Krichene and Rendle: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can yield model comparisons differing from full-catalog evaluation, including in expectation.
limitations: Does not prescribe changing the pinned RecHarness evaluator.
Does not determine the direction or size of any discrepancy for this intervention.

related_work.title: The Reusable Holdout: Preserving Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis
contributions: Explains how adaptive reuse of validation information can compromise generalization claims.
Supports recording the selection process and distinguishing exploratory validation results from final held-out assessment.
limitations: Recording trials or fixing seed 42 does not remove adaptive selection bias.
The proposed descriptive bootstrap does not implement a reusable-holdout mechanism or correct winner's optimism.
